chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Qummi from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Amira, raising it, said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed by a man who was praying the forenoon prayer in the Mosque of Kufa, so he pressed his side with the whip and said: 'You slaughtered the prayer of the repentant, may Allah slaughter you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So shall I leave it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'What is your view of the one who forbids a servant when he is praying?' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'And the denial of Ali (peace be upon him) is sufficient for its forbiddance.'

key_terms.نَحَرْتَ: You slaughtered (metaphor for wasting or improperly performing)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the forenoon prayer (Salat al-Duha) according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) encounters a man praying the forenoon (Duha) prayer in Kufa and gently nudges him, remarking that he has 'slaughtered' the prayer of the penitent, implying it was rushed or done without due reverence. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses this incident to establish a key jurisprudential principle: the mere act of correcting or lightly reprimanding a voluntary prayer does not constitute a prohibition, thereby validating the practice of Duha as a recommended (mustahabb) act rather than a disliked one.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Al-Qummy, from Ali Bin Al-Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, raising it, said,

‘Amir Al-Momineenasws passed by a man who was praying the forenoon Salāt in Masjid Al-Kufa. So heasws pressed his side by the whip and said: ‘You slaughtered the Salāt of the repentant, may Allahazwj Slaughter you’. Heasws said: ‘So shall I leave it?’ So heasws said: ‘What is your view of those who forbid a servant when he is praying Salāt?’ So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘And the denial of Aliasws is sufficient for its forbiddance’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il al-Qummiy from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following:

“’Amir al-Mu’minin once passed by a man who was performing al-Duha’ (optional Salah (prayer) at noontime before Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime) in Masjid of al-Kufah. He (’Amir al-Mu’minin) poked his side with his whip (handle) and said, ‘You cut the throat of the Salah (prayer) of repenting people, may Allah cut your throat.’ He asked, ‘Must I omit it? He (the Imam) said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin said, “Have you seen the one who forbids a servant who performs Salah (prayer)” (96:9,10) he added.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘The denial of Amir al- Mu’minin is sufficient prohibition to perform such Salah (prayer).”’ (’Amir al-Mu’minin meant that it is not permissible to prohibit Salah (prayer) but Salah (prayer) of a prescribed time performed before its time is not a Salah (prayer). (It seems the man performed the optional Salah (prayer) soon after Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime) before its due time).
